To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) BYV methyltransferases and helicases were detected by monoclonal antibodies and were found in the membrane fraction, and (ii), in the BYV 295 kDa protein, the leader papain proteinase cleaves the 1a polyprotein to produce two fragments, 66 and 229 kDA, but the 1a product undergoes additional processing.

the methyltransferase (ORF 1a product) and helicases (ORF 2 and 3 product) of beet yellows virus (BYV), a positive-stranded RNA virus, are associated with the membrane fractions of BYV infected plants.
(i) The 1a protein of BYV, which encodes a methyltransferase and a helicase, undergoes additional cleavage in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of MAbs to the viral proteins, and the detection of the viral proteins in vivo using these MAbs.
the development of a new set of MAbs against two conserved regions of the 1a polyprotein of BYV, which may be useful for the detection of the viral proteins in vivo.
the development of MAbs against the 1a and 1b proteins of BYV, which will be useful in the study of the structure and function of these proteins and their roles in the virus life cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 1a polyprotein is cleaved into at least five products: the leader protein, the methyltransferase, the helicase, and the two proteins of unknown function, which are probably involved in RNA replication.
the 295 kDa BYV 1A polyprotein, like other closterovirus 1A polyproteins, undergoes a complex proteolytic processing that is not well understood at the present time.
the BYV MT-like protein is a 63 kDa polypeptide that is cleaved by an as yet uncharacterized proteinase, whereas the BYV HEL-like protein is a approximately 100-kDa polypeptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BYV 5'-terminal 1a protein is processed in vivo by a virus-encoded and/or cellular proteinase into a 63 kDa MT-like protein and a 100 kDa HEL-like protein.
the closterovirus 1a protein is processed into the methyltransferase and the helicases, which may be associated with the membranes and/or the large organelles of the infected cells.
we have developed MAbs against the BYV MT-like and HEL-like proteins and have shown that they are present in the infected plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 1a polyprotein is proteolytically processed in the infected cells, and the resulting products are localized in the membrane fractions of the cells.

the BYV 63 kDa and 100 kDa proteins are associated with membranes, and that the 1a polyprotein is processed into the 1a, 1a-1, and 1a-2 fragments, in addition to the 1a-3 and 1a-N fragments that are produced by the leader papin-like cysteine protease.
we have developed the first set of MAbs against the 1a product that are suitable for detection and localization of the BYV MT and HEL proteins in vivo.
